html:
The Clatsop are a Chinookan-speaking people of the north-western Oregon coast, from the mouth of the Columbia River south to Tillamook Head. They were close neighbours and kin of the Chinook across the river.

They lived in cedar plank houses, fished salmon and sturgeon, and gathered shellfish and roots. They took part in the trade of the lower Columbia, where the Chinook Jargon became a common trading language. In the winter of 1805 to 1806 the Lewis and Clark Expedition built Fort Clatsop near their villages and traded with their chief Coboway. Epidemics in the following decades killed most of the Clatsop. Today their descendants are part of the Chinook Indian Nation, which is still seeking federal recognition. To the south lived the Tillamook.
